title: Project Northstar automatic-merge decision map
question: Should Project Northstar enable automatic merging for AI-generated dependency updates during the next four-week release cycle?
verdict: Provisional decision: do not enable the proposed automatic-merging rule for AI-generated dependency updates in the next four-week release cycle. The evidence supports potential benefit for a narrowly tested low-risk patch cohort, but does not cover the rule's current security surfaces or recovery capability.

nodes.label: Do not enable the proposed rule this cycle
nodes.text: Project Northstar should not enable its current automatic-merging rule for AI-generated dependency updates during the next four-week release cycle.

nodes.label: A limited cohort showed promise
nodes.text: Required checks caught both failures in a synthetic replay of low-risk patch updates, so automation may be viable for that tested cohort.

nodes.label: Replay evidence has a material boundary
nodes.text: The controlled replay does not establish safety for major updates, install scripts, or authentication and authorization changes.

nodes.label: Routine review creates delivery delay
nodes.text: The recorded routine patch-update review wait is a reason to consider automation, if safety conditions are met.

nodes.label: Controlled replay passed 18 of 20 updates
nodes.text: In the synthetic replay, 18 of 20 low-risk patch updates passed the complete test suite without manual edits; the two failures were detected before merge by required checks.

nodes.label: Replay excluded higher-risk change types
nodes.text: The replay did not include major-version updates, packages with install scripts, or changes to authentication and authorization code.

nodes.label: Generated descriptions lack signed provenance
nodes.text: There is no signed provenance record for generated pull-request descriptions, so a reviewer cannot verify from a description alone which model, prompt, or retrieved advisory produced a recommendation.

nodes.label: Current rule leaves sensitive surfaces eligible
nodes.text: The proposed rule currently excludes neither packages with install scripts nor updates that touch the authentication directory.

nodes.label: Routine reviews waited 31 hours
nodes.text: The synthetic team recorded a median wait of 31 hours for routine patch-update review during the previous four-week cycle.

nodes.label: No automatic-merge rollback drill is recorded
nodes.text: No rollback drill has been recorded for an automatically merged dependency update, and the fixture contains no measurement of recovery time after a bad merge.

nodes.label: Rollback readiness is unmeasured
nodes.text: It is unknown whether a bad automatically merged dependency update can be detected and recovered within an acceptable time; this could change the decision if demonstrated for the proposed rule.

edges.note: The replay directly shows required checks catching the two observed failures within the low-risk patch cohort.
This favorable result is limited to the tested cohort, so it narrows rather than overturns the decision against the broader proposed rule.
The stated exclusions directly delimit what the replay can establish.
Because the proposed rule covers surfaces absent from the replay, the replay cannot justify enabling that rule as written.
Missing signed provenance prevents verification of the generation inputs from the pull-request description, which is a reason not to rely on automated merges yet.
Allowing install-script and authentication-directory changes conflicts with the replay boundary, leaving the current rule without relevant safety evidence.
The recorded 31-hour median wait directly establishes an operational cost of the current manual review process.
A substantial routine-review wait is a reason to enable automation, pushing against the provisional decision not to enable it.
The absence of a recorded drill and recovery-time measurement is the observed basis for the unresolved rollback-readiness gap.
A demonstrated, acceptable recovery capability could reduce the risk of enabling the rule; without it, the decision remains provisional and conservative.
